Grace / team —

I ran a quick sensitivity matrix against the token distribution Alice provided. Notes and assumptions up front:
- Model baseline: open-llama-13B (FP16) and q4_0 quantized variant as a fallback
- Measured local perf (A100 80GB equivalent): ~1,800 tokens/sec for steady-state single-request streaming (p50) at 512 context. For p95 behavior with bursts and smaller batch windows, per-GPU *effective* sustained tokens/sec ~1,100 TPS (conservative)
- H100/Higher-end inference kernel gives ~35% higher tokens/sec in our kernel bench (so ~1,500 effective p95 TPS/GPU) but at higher cost and less availability for Dedicated.

Mapping to ClientX peaks:
- Peak sustained tokens/sec estimate = peak_qps * mean_tokens/request = 220 * 120 = 26,400 tokens/sec
- If we size to meet peak p95 with A100-equivalent GPUs (1,100 TPS/GPU p95) => raw GPU count = ceil(26,400 / 1,100) = 24 GPUs
- That yields headroom = (24 * 1,100 - 26,400) / 26,400 = ~0% (no headroom). To reach ~40% headroom we'd need 34 GPUs (~34 * 1,100 = 37,400 tokens/sec)

With H100-equivalent runtime (1,500 TPS/GPU p95):
- Raw GPUs for peak = ceil(26,400 / 1,500) = 18 GPUs
- 40% headroom target => ~25 GPUs

Recommendations (two commits to present):
- Conservative commit (cost-focused): 18 A100-eq GPUs + autoscale/burst capacity policy to H100 spare pool for peaks — expected p95 fit with modest fallbacks; expected headroom ~18% during typical peaks
- Aggressive commit (performance-first): 25 A100-eq GPUs (or 18 H100-eq) — meets p95 at peak with ~40% headroom and fewer fallback events

I've attached the capacity workbook (capacity_model_clientx_v1.xlsx) with the detailed per-slab TPS, cost per token estimates, and latency margin columns (batch-size sensitivity, quantization delta).

Open questions for pricing/legal:
- Do we need an explicit SLA with credit tiers tied to p95 latency? If so, we'll model credit exposure under the proposed commits.
- Preferred start date? Ramp profile (instant vs 30-day ramp) changes cost and available headroom significantly.

Karthik
Applied ML / Inference Performance
(attachment: capacity_model_clientx_v1.xlsx)
